title: Redwood migration demo: OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood
next_steps: Share parity mapping doc and sample migration guide
Schedule infra benchmark (seed 100K tokens) with Jordan
Provide pricing comparison sheet for hosted vs dedicated
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-28
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60m
Attendees: Emily Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood Product), Carlos Mendes (CTO, BrightEdge), Priya Kapoor (ML Eng), Liam O'Neill (Head of Security), Sara Kim (PM)

Summary: quick demo focused on migration parity (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood), API mappings, console walkthrough for rollouts/Optimize recommendations, and security questions (VPC, KMS). Agreed next steps: security pack, parity doc, benchmark run, pricing sheet.

[00:00] Emily Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about an hour, i'll do a quick intro then jordan will jump into a live demo of the api parity and the console. 
[00:12] Carlos Mendes: thanks emily, yeah we've got priya and liam on, priya is going to drive the technical questions, liam will look at security. we use OpenAI primarily and some Anthropic experiments, also testing Together models. main ask is migration with minimal code change and cost predictability.
[00:28] Jordan Lee: great, so i'll start with a mapping high-level then show live calls. first: api surface. Redwood has a unified endpoint for completions/chat, embeddings, plus function calling and streaming. code-level it's very similar to openai, e.g. post /v1/responses or /v1/embeddings, but we include model aliasing and more explicit routing controls.
[00:45] Priya Kapoor: can you show how streaming compares? we use streaming for low-latency UI.
[00:52] Jordan Lee: absolutely. watch this  i'm sending a streaming chat request to a gpt-like variant. you'll notice chunked events show up, same pattern as openai but with slightly different event names in the sdk (RWD.stream). we also have automatic prefix cache and kv cache reuse for chat sessions which reduces repeat-token cost; some customers call it kv cash in notes, ha.
[01:18] [screen share starts] Jordan Lee: (typing) code snippet: axios.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses", {model: "redwood/gpt-1.2", input: "Summarize..."})  here you can see response streaming and also a 'model_variant' field returned. that helps when we route to a quantized variant for cost.
[01:42] Priya Kapoor: when you say model_variant, can we pin to an exact op-model? we have latency sensitive endpoints.
[01:48] Jordan Lee: yes you can pin version or set fallback rules. in the console you can create a route that pins to 'redwood/gpt-1.2:2025-11-05' or set policy: prefer_hosted, fallback: dedicated-quantized.
[02:10] Carlos Mendes: how does this map to anthropic's api? we use Claude for some safety tasks.
[02:15] Maya Ortiz: good question  parity doc maps 'Claude-instruct' calls to our instruct optimized models and we expose sanitized system instruction controls so you can reproduce prompt-scoped safety. we sent an initial parity spreadsheet (link in chat) but i'll walk through the key rows live.
[02:36] [Jordan scrolls] Jordan Lee: here: openai/chat.completions -> redwood/responses, openai embeddings -> redwood/embeddings, anthropic's 'assistant' roles map to our system/assistant role with role-preserve flag. Together.ai model names map to 'redwood/together-compat' variants which maintain tokenizer and logits for parity.
[02:59] Priya Kapoor: tokenization differences worry me  will embeddings be compatible for our vector DB? we've got an existing index built on OpenAI embeddings.
[03:10] Jordan Lee: embeddings are a common ask. Redwood offers an 'embedding_compat' mode that aims to match OpenAI's embedding outputs for specific model families where feasible; we also provide a migration script that recomputes vectors in batches and a soft-join strategy so you can keep your index consistent during rollout. we'll share the script.
[03:34] Liam O'Neill: on security  our compliance is strict. SOC2 plus we have SSO, KMS, customer-managed keys. can you speak to private deployments and audit logs?
[03:44] Emily Chen: sure  Redwood Private supports VPC peering and an on-prem package for air-gapped. for hosted customers we offer envelope encryption with CMKs (KMS) and HSM integration as an enterprise add-on. audit logs are retained per route and you can stream them to your SIEM. i'll add the compliance pack to next steps.
[04:10] Liam O'Neill: do you support SAML/SSO for user access and RBAC for console?
[04:14] Maya Ortiz: yes  SSO via SAML, OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access. we can limit who can create routes or change rollouts. also we surface token-level spend and per-route cost to help internal chargeback.
[04:28] Sara Kim: curious about Redwood Optimize  you mentioned batch settings and quantization suggestions earlier. how prescriptive is it?
[04:37] Jordan Lee: Optimize analyzes request patterns and suggests batching windows, cache TTLs, and model suggestions. e.g., for embeddings-heavy workloads it may recommend a lower-precision embedding variant with negligible quality drop and 30% cost savings. it's a recommendations engine plus simulation; you can apply suggestions automatically in staging only.
[05:05] [05:05] Jordan Lee: demo: console -> routes -> create route -> attach model profile -> rollout config (canary 5% -> 20% -> full). you can also add quality gates (evals tied to prompt sets) so if regression is detected we auto-roll back. customers love that for cautious migrations.
[05:35] Priya Kapoor: speak to latency numbers  our SLA is 200ms for short prompts.
[05:39] Jordan Lee: latency depends on model and deployment mode. Hosted gpt-like served on proximate region typically 60-200ms for small contexts; Dedicated with pinned GPUs gets consistent p99s for higher throughput. we can provide benchmarks for your prompt shapes  that's why we propose a 100k token benchmark run.
[06:05] Carlos Mendes: cost predictability  we want to avoid runaway spend that we saw during a promo last quarter. how does rate limiting and quotas work?
[06:13] Maya Ortiz: console has per-token quotas, rate limits, and alerting. you can set hard caps per org or per route, and see projected spend. for Dedicated we offer reserved units with monthly commit pricing which evens out spend spikes.
[06:32] [06:32] Priya Kapoor: can we keep some workloads on OpenAI and others on Redwood during migration?
[06:35] Jordan Lee: absolutely  smart routing policies let you route by tag, latency, cost, or user. you'll often do a canary with 5-10% traffic routed to Redwood, evaluate quality and cost, then ramp.
[06:50] Carlos Mendes: show error modes and graceful degradation  what happens if a model is overloaded?
[06:55] Jordan Lee: two approaches: fallback to a cheaper quantized variant or fallback to another region/model. we also have automatic retry policies and circuit-breakers. you'll get observability traces for tokens and model latency in the console.
[07:12] [screen: logs view] Jordan Lee: here is a trace view  token-level breakdown, which route, which model-variant served. note the bucketed cost estimates on each request row.
[07:31] Liam O'Neill: for audit we need immutable logs and export to our GCS bucket. can logs be pushed?
[07:37] Emily Chen: yes logs can be forwarded to S3/GCS/our SIEM webhook. we can also provide time-limited signed exports for legal review.
[07:50] Priya Kapoor: about function calling  we heavily use it for structured outputs. how's parity?
[07:55] Jordan Lee: function calling is supported; we have a minor difference in how we signal partial outputs in streaming and function name resolution, but the SDK wraps most of it so migrations are minimal. there are a couple of edge cases  we'll include them in the parity doc.
[08:15] Sara Kim: any known gotchas moving from Together models? we used Together for local fine-tuning.
[08:21] Jordan Lee: Together compatibility layer preserves tokenizer and logits where required; however fine-tuned tokens may need re-quant or a short retrain for low-rank adapters. we recommend a small smoke test to validate alignment.
[08:45] [08:45] Carlos Mendes: can you share the parity mapping doc now?
[08:48] Maya Ortiz: yes  dropped into chat: https://redwood.ai/docs/parity/brightedge (mock link). it includes example curl/snippets for OpenAI -> Redwood and Anthropic -> Redwood.
[09:02] Priya Kapoor: ok let's talk migration plan: number one, low-risk path is embeddings migration with reindexing; second, chat endpoints with canary; third, full cutover for non-critical routes. timeline  we want a pilot in 4 weeks.
[09:17] Emily Chen: sounds good  we can run a benchmark in week 1, then pilot for 2-3 weeks, then rollout. Jordan will own the benchmark run, i'll own commercial/pricing, maya will handle product config/optimize.
[09:34] Liam O'Neill: contractual questions  data residency and deletion policies?
[09:39] Maya Ortiz: we support region pinning for hosted. data retention settings per customer, and deletion endpoints plus proof-of-deletion for enterprise plans. we'll include the legal/contact to go over contract terms.
[09:55] [09:55] Carlos Mendes: you mentioned cost savings with quantization. what's typical?
[09:59] Jordan Lee: depends  for many workloads 2-4x token throughput improvement with 4-bit quantized variants and associated 30-60% cost reduction on those routes, but quality-sensitive tasks might not be good candidates. Optimize helps pick which ones.
[10:18] Priya Kapoor: last technical  can we run a side-by-side eval for quality (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding similarity)?
[10:23] Jordan Lee: yes, the evals pipeline can run your prompt sets against both systems and produce diffs and regression alerts. we'll attach a sample eval harness.
[10:35] [wrap-up] Emily Chen: recap  action items: 1) Jordan: run 100k token benchmark (w/ priya) and share results (week 1) 2) Emily: send security pack and pricing sheet (48 hrs) 3) Maya: parity mapping doc + migration guide (today) 4) schedule pilot kickoff (tentative week 4).
[10:58] Carlos Mendes: good call, thanks everyone. we'll review the security pack and follow up with availability for the benchmark.
[11:05] Jordan Lee: thanks all, i'll follow up with notes and links to the demo artifacts.

Notes / artifacts referenced: parity spreadsheet (link), security/compliance deck (link), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared), sample migration scripts (repo link).

Transcript quirks: minor ASR mistakes (Redwood Optimize -> Redwood Optimise), occasional overlap/cross-talk, some product names slightly mis-transcribed.
